items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: many, many, many times Ellington would call him up from out on the road, 'Sweetpea, I want an arrangement on so and so and so and so.' ... And that was Strayhorn

ctx.x: I remember hearing him tell Duke that he had been playing, "Take the A Train" wrong. For a long, long time and he -- this was on a television show he did with Ralph Gleason he did for educational television, in San Francisco. And he played it the way, he said, "I wrote it, Edward," and he said "you haven't been playing it that way for a long time".

That's right, he was a very meticulous little fellow. And he was right in most everything he did. And many, many, many times Ellington would call him up from out on the road, "Sweetpea, I want an arrangement on so and so and so and so." Well, when do you need it? In a couple

of days, so -- and Sweetpea, "All right." And in a couple of days the most gorgeous arrangement on that particular piece. And that was Strayhorn and he never got the credit, I mean, he was always feeling that well, isn't that nice that this fellow took this little boy and give him such a nice chance? Oh, no, that's -- you're entirely wrong. He was the genius, the power behind that throne all of those latter years. He was terrific.
